newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Q1 mortgage lending up 41 pct from Q4.
newsitem.headline: Danish Q1 mortgage lending up 41 pct from Q4.

text.p: Danish mortgage companies lent about 52 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1997, sharply up from around 37 billion in the last three months of 1996, lenders said on Tuesday.

"Demand for mortgages rose in the first quarter of 1997 after a decline at the end of 1996. In comparison to the last quarter of 1996 there were rises in gross lending for all property types," the Realkreditradet lenders' association said.
A Realkreditradet statement said that lending for owner-occupied properties and holiday homes accounted for 28 billion crowns of the first quarter total.
Net lending was 15 billion crowns in the 1997 first quarter, compared to seven billion during the last three months of 1996, it added. --Eva Elgaard Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969655
